messages.author: 4b06c0bae2d1991d
messages.subject: lavaanList vs lavaan.mi
parts:
I'm running a model with cfa.mi() but when I try to get the results with summary() it won't accept any of the arguments specified on the class?lavaan.mi page, but instead takes the arguments from the class?lavaanList page (e.g. header, estimates). 

Any idea why its trying to use the wrong methods??

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaanList vs lavaan.mi
parts: Any idea why its trying to use the wrong methods?

No, but someone else had this issue too, and we never resolved it.  All I can suggest is trying to (re)install the latest R and the latest development versions of lavaan and semTools.

https://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki

After restarting R, check your sessionInfo() output to verify R(Studio) is not loading any other packages unexpectedly that might be interfering with the namespace search path.  Then, load semTools and run the ?runMI help-page examples to check whether the same problem occurs.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Thanks Terrence - 

FWIW, I re-installed as suggested and if I run my code top-to-bottom, I still have this problem, but if run the example on runMI, I get the correct results. One thing I noticed is that when I run my code, I see this as the methods:

> showMethods(f=summary,classes='lavaan.mi')
Function: summary (package base)
object="lavaan.mi"
    (inherited from: object="lavaanList")

But with runMI in a new session, I have this:

> showMethods(f=summary,classes='lavaan.mi')
Function: summary (package base)
object="lavaan.mi"


I don't know enough about inheritance of methods, but somehow it is inheriting the method in my longer code and not in the example.

messages.subject: Re: lavaanList vs lavaan.mi
parts:
lavaan.mi does inherit from lavaanList, as explained on the class?lavaan.mi help page.  It basically means I take the lavaanList class, then add some of my own slots necessary for the multiple-imputation functionality.  So in any case you should see this is TRUE:

inherits(fit, "lavaanList")
